sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's energy transition hinges on PLN's capex cycle and feed-in tariff revisions, making policy clarity the dominant swing factor for local renewables valuations.
US solar demand is structurally supported by IRA subsidies and grid-scale backlog, insulating SEDG/ENPH from near-term rate volatility.
Climate-tech capital is bifurcating: US equipment makers benefit from reshoring incentives, while Indonesian developers face currency and offtake risks that cap upside.
sectors.ai: US-listed renewables rebounded on rate-cut hopes while Indonesian names lagged on rupiah weakness and policy uncertainty. Buy US solar equipment (SEDG, ENPH) for near-term beta, but rotate into Indonesian utilities (HGII) only after clarity on PLN procurement and tariff reform. Hedge IDR exposure via NRG-style cash-flow names.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Structural premium on export-oriented FMCG names (e.g., BIKE, POLU) as IDR weakness boosts competitiveness in regional markets, a durable driver independent of domestic consumption.
Consolidation in mid-cap consumer sub-sectors (AGAR, VISI) is accelerating as smaller players gain share via digital distribution, creating persistent M&A and rerating opportunities.
Regulatory shifts on halal certification and local-content rules are raising barriers to entry, benefiting established players with compliance infrastructure (AMMS, AEGS) over the long term.
sectors.ai: Consumer & FMCG is in a WATCH phase with aggregate -0.84%, but the sharp rallies in BIKE, POLU, AGAR, and VISI signal selective speculative momentum, not broad strength. Favor exporters and niche players with earnings catalysts; avoid index-heavy staples until IDX volume confirms a reversal. Position tactically in high-beta names with tight stops, as domestic demand remains soft ahead of rate decisions.

Rotate from US-exposed plays into domestic ID beneficiaries as rupiah stabilizes and Jokowi's successor front-loads infrastructure spending.
